rows.title: Feds Say Self-Driving Uber SUV Did Not Recognize Jaywalking Pedestrian In Fatal Crash
rows.standfirst: The death of a pedestrian struck by the self-driving vehicle in Arizona last year highlights safety concerns and calls for regulating the testing of such vehicles.

rows.title: Your Secret Score
rows.standfirst: It's no secret that every online platform you use is keeping track of your information. But what if this data is being used to give you a 'score' as a customer?

rows.title: U.S. Company Accused Of Illegally Selling Chinese-Made Security Products To Military
rows.standfirst: Aventura Technologies Inc. and seven of its employees are facing charges of fraud, money laundering and illegal importation of Chinese equipment, which officials say endangered military personnel.

rows.title: German Airline Lufthansa Grounds 1,300 Flights As Flight Attendants Strike
rows.standfirst: Thousands of employees picketed outside of airports in Germany. Lufthansa, that nation's largest carrier, expects 180,000 passengers will be affected by the two-day work stoppage.

rows.title: Las Vegas Bans Sleeping, Camping in Public Places
rows.standfirst: Homeless activists swarmed the Las Vegas City Council chambers chanting, "Housing, not handcuffs!" The mayor said the measure is necessary in order to address a homeless problem that is not abating.

rows.title: Post-#MeToo, Ernst & Young Grapples With Diverging Views Of Its Culture
rows.standfirst: Until recently, the accounting giant coached some top women leaders to look "polished" and speak briefly. The company has since disavowed the program, arguing its workplace culture promotes women.

rows.title: 'The Mysterious Affair At Olivetti' Attempts To Find A Cold War Conspiracy
rows.standfirst: Biographer Meryle Secrest chases a theory that two key Olivetti computer visonaries' deaths did not happen as officially recorded. While a gripping read at times, there's not a lot of solid ground.

rows.title: Despite Bankruptcy And Illness, Bob Murray Remains A Loud Voice For Coal
rows.standfirst: Bob Murray rose from coal miner to executive and became an influential industry voice. Despite his role in crafting the Trump administration's pro-coal policies, his own company is bankrupt.

rows.title: A Ban On High-Cost Loans May Be Coming
rows.standfirst: Some payday loans carry interest rates of 100% or more. The Military Lending Act limits rates on loans to service members. Now, a bipartisan bill aims to extend that protection to all Americans.

rows.title: Boeing CEO Says He Decided Not To Quit After 737 Max Crashes And Gave Up Bonuses
rows.standfirst: "I don't see running away from a challenge, resigning, as the right solution," Dennis Muilenburg said. A lawmaker asked him if he was taking a cut in pay, prompting the CEO to give up his bonuses.

rows.title: What's The Beef? The Declining American Leather Industry
rows.standfirst: The leather manufacturing industry was once a backbone of the American economy. Now the industry is in decline, and the trade war isn't helping.

rows.title: Under New Deal, Australian Women's And Men's Soccer Will Get Equal Share Of Revenue
rows.standfirst: The deal will lift salaries for the Matildas by 90% and promises parity in training and travel. Norway and New Zealand have made similar moves, as a lawsuit against U.S. Soccer continues.

rows.title: FCC Clears T-Mobile/Sprint Merger Deal
rows.standfirst: The next hurdle is a federal trial in December in which a coalition of state attorneys general are challenging the merger as anti-competitive.

rows.title: ABC News Defends Its Epstein Coverage After Leaked Video Of Anchor
rows.standfirst: On the video, anchor Amy Robach complains that ABC News "quashed" her interview with a Jeffrey Epstein accuser, suggesting the network yielded to threats from powerful forces.

rows.title: Openness Versus National Security: A Dilemma For U.S. Schools
rows.standfirst: Last year, the Education Department reported that U.S. universities received over $1.3 billion dollars in the form of gifts and contracts. Most of this money came from China.

rows.title: Amazon Appeals Pentagon's Choice Of Microsoft For $10 Billion Cloud Contract
rows.standfirst: Amazon cited "unmistakable bias" as it prepares to challenge its loss in federal court. This starts a new chapter in the contentious battle over the biggest U.S. cloud-computing contract, called JEDI.

rows.title: Winning The Nobel
rows.standfirst: Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee talk about their work and what happens when you win a Nobel Prize.

rows.title: Federal Appeals Court Allows Congress To Subpoena Trump Tax Returns
rows.standfirst: The full D.C. Circuit voted 8-3 not to reconsider an earlier decision by a three-judge panel that ruled against the president. Trump's lawyer says he will appeal to the Supreme Court.

rows.title: Politics And The Trade War
rows.standfirst: Did President Trump's trade policies cost Republican votes last year? We talk to economist Chad Bown to find out.

rows.title: What Happens To Your Used Stuff? 'Secondhand' Tells Of A Billion-Dollar Industry
rows.standfirst: As "traditional bonds disintegrate in the face of industrialization, urbanization, and secularization, brands and objects become a means to curate and project who we are," writes reporter Adam Minter.

rows.title: The Great Cranberry Scare Of 1959
rows.standfirst: Sixty years ago, a food scare nearly crushed the cranberry business. Cranberries have bounced back since then, but the industry is facing new threats.

rows.title: McDonald's Is Sued Over 'Systemic Sexual Harassment' Of Female Workers
rows.standfirst: A former employee has filed a class-action lawsuit against McDonald's and one Michigan franchise, alleging a "culture of sexual harassment."

rows.title: Trump Makes No Promises On China Trade Deal
rows.standfirst: President Trump says a mini trade agreement with China could happen "soon," but he offered no guarantees. In a speech to the Economic Club of New York, Trump downplayed the cost of his trade war.

rows.title: Supreme Court Allows Sandy Hook Families' Case Against Remington Arms To Proceed
rows.standfirst: The gun-maker had appealed to the highest federal court after the Connecticut Supreme Court allowed the lawsuit over the 2012 school massacre in Newtown, Conn., to go forward in March.

rows.title: Charitable Giving Is Down. It Might Be Time To Reform The Charitable Deduction.
rows.standfirst: It's distortionary. It's regressive. And right now it only benefits a sliver of taxpayers and nonprofits. It's time to talk about the charitable deduction.

rows.title: My Journey Into The World Of Men's Beauty
rows.standfirst: Makeup was once thought to be the exclusive realm of women, but more and more men are experimenting with cosmetics — and the industry is taking notice. A reporter gives it a try.

rows.title: Why Sam Sanders Is Binging 'Friends'
rows.standfirst: Netflix, HBO, Amazon, Hulu, Disney, NBC, they're all at war for your eyeballs. Today on the show, the streaming wars. Who the major players are, what's at stake and what it will mean for you.

rows.title: A Smart Home Neighborhood: Residents Find It Enjoyably Convenient Or A Bit Creepy
rows.standfirst: Smart homes let homeowners turn on lights and unlock doors from a mobile phone. But the technology also sends incredible amounts of data to big tech companies.

rows.title: The Lancaster, Pa., Puzzle
rows.standfirst: A heavily rural county with a big manufacturing base and a low share of college graduates has found a way to thrive.

rows.title: With Blackouts, California's Electric Car Owners Are Finding New Ways To Charge Up
rows.standfirst: Nearly half of all the electric cars in the country are owned in California. But the recent wildfires and power outages are inspiring some drivers to use their cars to power their homes.

rows.title: 'It's Going To Get Worse': How U.S. Countertop Workers Started Getting Sick
rows.standfirst: The story of the first worker in the U.S. to suffer lung damage after cutting a new kind of countertop material shows the way a workplace hazard emerged in this country.

rows.title: Ready Your Wallet For Thanksgiving Dinner
rows.standfirst: What will Thanksgiving dinner cost you this year? Also, Cardiff brings back the debate on which is better, pumpkin or pecan pie.

rows.title: McDonald's Failed To Protect Workers Against Violent Customers, Lawsuit Says
rows.standfirst: A lawsuit by 17 McDonald's workers recounts threats, harassment and assaults, accusing the fast-food chain of "undermining safety" with late-night work, store design changes and inadequate training.

rows.title: Disney Animation Chief Jennifer Lee Is The Queen Behind Elsa And Anna
rows.standfirst: Her credits include Frozen , Wreck-It Ralph and Zootopia . Now, Jennifer Lee is the first female chief creative officer of Walt Disney Animation Studios — oh, and she co-directed the Frozen sequel.

rows.title: 2020 Affordable Care Act Health Plans: What's New
rows.standfirst: ACA plans for 2020 are cheaper than last year — premiums lower, on average. And in some areas, people who qualify for federal subsidies could end up with no monthly payment. But read the fine print.

rows.title: UAW President Gary Jones Abruptly Resigns Amid Corruption Scandal
rows.standfirst: Jones has been the target of a federal probe of alleged corruption in the UAW. The union is also linked to an alleged bribery scheme, according to a lawsuit filed by GM against rival Fiat Chrysler.

rows.title: Lancaster Spotlight, Part 2: A Refugee's Tale
rows.standfirst: In our second spotlight episode on Lancaster County, we look into what Lancaster's success can tell us about the relationship between refugees and the local economy.

rows.title: Companies Try To Trademark 'Ok, Boomer' Expression
rows.standfirst: Now that the expression "OK, Boomer" has gone viral, companies are trying to cash in on the meme's moment. Some hope to make a business line of it by trademarking the phrase.

rows.title: As Oil Prices Drop And Money Dries Up, Is The U.S. Shale Boom Going Bust?
rows.standfirst: The boom that helped make the U.S. the world's largest oil producer could be ending. Oil prices are down amid weak demand, and investors no longer seem willing to write the industry a blank check.

rows.title: California Governor Cracks Down On Fracking, Requires Audits And Scientific Review
rows.standfirst: Gavin Newsom's initiatives follow a massive oil release from a Chevron facility in Kern County suspected of being caused by a high-pressure steam process for releasing oil from underground rock.

rows.title: Gordon Sondland Was A Low-Profile Hotel Owner. Until He Went To Work For Trump
rows.standfirst: The Portland hotel owner and ambassador, who is scheduled to testify before Congress on Wednesday, is a pivotal witness in the impeachment inquiry. His relationship with Trump is a complicated one.

rows.title: U.S. Arrests Money-Laundering Expert For Laundering Money
rows.standfirst: A slew of federal agencies and media outlets have relied on professor Bruce Bagley's expertise on organized crime. This week he was arrested for his alleged role in an elaborate corruption scheme.

rows.title: Grocery Store Wars
rows.standfirst: The profit margin for groceries is razor thin. To stay competitive against increasingly large competitors like Amazon Prime, retailers are turning to a new service: curbside pickup.

rows.title: Want New Taxes To Pay For Health Care? Lessons From The Affordable Care Act
rows.standfirst: When passing the ACA, Democrats touted the fact that they had included many measures to pay for the bill's expanded coverage. But nearly 10 years later, Congress has eliminated many of those taxes.

rows.title: How Does The Economy Influence Voters?
rows.standfirst: The economy is one of the most important factors in how people vote. But its influence has been changing and it has everything to do with politics.

rows.title: UAW Reaches Tentative Labor Agreement With Fiat Chrysler
rows.standfirst: The tentative agreement makes Fiat Chrysler the last of the big three Detroit automakers to arrive at a deal with the United Auto Workers this year.

rows.title: Doorbusters Busted: Shoppers Rethink Black Friday
rows.standfirst: The day after Thanksgiving is still the busiest shopping day of the year. But, for many reasons, it is losing its status as the focal point of the holiday shopping season.

rows.title: Following Backlash, Twitter Offers to 'Memorialize' Accounts Of The Deceased
rows.standfirst: The company received criticism over plans to delete inactive accounts. It later clarified that deletions will not occur until after a "memorial" function is introduced.

rows.title: Massive Explosion Rips Through Texas Chemical Plant
rows.standfirst: The blast is the latest in a string of industrial incidents in east Texas. The explosion at the petrochemical plant injured three people and blew out windows and mangled doors of some nearby homes.

rows.title: The Sahm Rule With The Eponymous Economist
rows.standfirst: Economist Claudia Sahm explains the eponymous Sahm Rule, and how changes in the unemployment rate point to whether or not we are in a recession.

rows.title: Choosing Not To Fly Home For The Holidays, For The Climate's Sake
rows.standfirst: Carbon emissions from global air travel are rising fast, and U.S. passengers make up the largest share. But some are vowing not to fly at all, motivated by guilt and concern for the environment.

rows.title: 99 Bottles Of Beer On The Touch Screen: The Spread Of Self-Serve Taps
rows.standfirst: Order a drink, but hold the bartender? As it becomes relatively more expensive to run restaurants and bars, some are saving money by replacing human servers with pour-your-own electronic taps.

rows.title: 737 Max Scandal Cuts Boeing's Once Rock-Solid Image
rows.standfirst: Boeing is grappling with more than just fixing the technical problems with its 737 Max planes. Two crashes of the new plane have undermined trust in the aircraft manufacturer.

rows.title: 'Highlights' Magazine Sticks To Winning Formula Of Mixing Fun With Learning
rows.standfirst: In the fast-paced ever-changing world of children's entertainment, Highlights magazine , founded in 1946, slows things down with short articles and puzzles.

rows.title: Niche Products In Our Grocery Stores
rows.standfirst: Niche food products at grocery stores have been getting more and more popular. But, what took so long?

rows.title: What's Wrong with the Saudi Aramco IPO?
rows.standfirst: The most profitable company in the world was supposed to make its international debut, listing public shares for the first time at a valuation of $2 trillion. Now it's staying local. What happened?

rows.title: T-Mobile Has A Trademark On Magenta, Demands An Insurance Company Stop Using It
rows.standfirst: The mobile phone carrier is serious about the color associated with its brand. Now, a legal dispute involving T-Mobile's parent is raising the question: Is it possible to own a color?

rows.title: Lighting Industry's Future Dims As Efficient LED Bulbs Take Over
rows.standfirst: More efficient lightbulbs are cheaper and longer-lasting than ever. But while that's good for consumers, it can be tough for an industry that's also facing shifting regulations.

rows.title: The $100 Million Apple
rows.standfirst: Next week, a new product will hit store shelves. It's been in development for 20 years and cost millions of dollars to bring to market. It's a new kind of apple. And the stakes are high.

rows.title: Charles Schwab To Buy TD Ameritrade, Creating Brokerage Behemoth
rows.standfirst: Changes are rippling through the financial services market as trade fees drop to zero. The merger will likely attract antitrust scrutiny, as the combined firms will hold $5 trillion in client assets.

frame: Up to15 visible Business-archive cards at four fixed weekly endpoints, restricted to each block; not a full-publication census
